name: Milemarker
label: Jade Tree
lede: A Chapel Hill collective that set its drums on fire, got banned from Cat's Cradle, moved to Chicago, made synth-punk records with Steve Albini for Jade Tree, and ended up in Germany without ever quite breaking up.

eras.title: Casio presets and lighter fluid
eras.text: Milemarker started in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, as a self-declared collective, not a band, making art-damaged hardcore out of synthesizers and slogans. It released records at a sprint on small labels and set its own stage on fire.

years.src: Indy Week (2005) · Jade Tree · Village Voice (2016) · Milemarker Bandcamp
years.h: Dave Laney, Al Burian and Ben Davis start Milemarker in Chapel Hill
years.p: Milemarker called itself sci-fi soundtrack music genetically spliced with [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]], and a collective rather than a band. Laney later said they were the art-damaged kids of the scene.
years.xp:
Jade Tree's bio lists the collective's other names: the Milemarker People's Liberation Army and the Milemarker Entertainment and Reprogramming Consulate. The rule was that revolutionary art should be danceable.

The Village Voice says the Casio presets alienated hardcore purists. The members had other outlets too: Laney edited the magazine Media Reader, and Burian wrote the zine Burn Collector.

years.h: Two Milemarker albums in one year: Non Plus Ultra and Future Isms
years.p: Milemarker released Non Plus Ultra on Paralogy and Future Isms on Stickfigure, plus the Receiver 7-inch on Clocked Out.

years.h: Milemarker splits a 7-inch with The Blood Brothers
years.p: Milemarker shared a 7-inch with Seattle's [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]], and also put out the Sex Jams 7-inch on Bloodlink and Changing Caring Humans on Stickfigure.

q: We were all setting everything on fire
years.h: Milemarker sets its stage on fire, and gets banned from Cat's Cradle
years.p: Ben Davis started it by soaking his drums in lighter fluid and lighting them mid-set. Soon members were breathing fire, and Milemarker was banned from Chapel Hill's Cat's Cradle after smashing a keyboard.
years.xp: Burian told the Village Voice the escalation came from everyone competing for attention. When Roby Newton joined, she built a rig to set her arms alight, and Indy Week says she performed topless in electrical tape among light boxes she had rigged herself.

eras.title: Chicago, Jade Tree and Albini
eras.text: Milemarker moved to Chicago, where its lighting tech became its singer and the synth records found a home on Jade Tree and Lovitt Records. By 2001 the band said it had gone from being a spectacle to being a band.

years.h: Frigid Forms Sell on Lovitt, recorded with Brian McTernan
years.p: Milemarker's breakthrough came out on Lovitt (LOV20), recorded at Salad Days Studio by Brian McTernan. Songs include Sex Jam One: Sexual Machinery and Server Error.
years.xp: The credits list Al Burian, Dave Laney, Ben Davis, Roby Newton and drummer Sean Husick. Jade Tree reissued it in 2002, which is why Milemarker's Bandcamp dates it February 2002. Burian later called it the record with the most solid aesthetic and message.
play: Internet Relay Chat with the Central Intelligence Agency

years.h: Milemarker leaves Chapel Hill for Chicago
years.p: Milemarker relocated to Chicago in 2000. Dave Laney told the Chicago Reader everyone had wanted out of North Carolina for a long time, and Chicago won by elimination.

years.h: Roby Newton goes from lighting tech to singer
years.p: [[Roby Newton|b8497e6d-09f9-4a5a-bab8-9a9496ae0af2]] joined Milemarker to run its lights and projections, then took over vocals and synthesizer. She was also a puppeteer who toured her own shows and animations.

years.src: Discogs · Creative Loafing (2010) · Chicago Reader (2001) · Roy Christopher
years.h: Anaesthetic: Milemarker's first full-length for Jade Tree
years.p: Recorded May 8 to 20, 2001, at Salad Days Studio in Washington, D.C., with Brian McTernan, and released as Jade Tree JT1061. The songs take on gentrification, sweatshops and terminal illness.
years.xp:
Al Burian said the album was first called Rise Up Friends, an animal-liberation concept the band dropped, and that three different drummers played on it. Demos were cut at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio.

The release party was at Chicago's Fireside Bowl.

years.h: Noah Leger of Hurl takes over the drums
years.p: The Chicago Reader listed [[Noah Leger|c8fd59fc-09db-4e77-9a67-749e5f47a3d6]], formerly of Hurl and Thee Speaking Canaries, as Milemarker's temporary drummer. He stayed through Ominosity.

years.h: Satanic Versus EP, three songs cut with Steve Albini
years.p: Jade Tree JT1078: three heavy songs recorded by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Electrical Audio on March 22 and 23, 2002, then electronic tracks the label compared to Kraftwerk and Prince.
years.xp: Noah Leger and Tim Herzog split the drums. Czech label Day After licensed a vinyl edition from Jade Tree. Pitchfork's Chris Ott reviewed it that October.

eras.title: A break that looked like a breakup
eras.text: In summer 2003 Milemarker stopped in a way the A.V. Club said looked more like a breakup. Two years later it came back with new blood, a Steve Albini recording and a harder, less synth-driven sound, just as synth-rock was getting popular.

years.h: Milemarker stops; Roby Newton leaves
years.p: Dave Laney and Al Burian put Milemarker aside in summer 2003 for a new band, and Roby Newton left. Ben Davis told Indy Week she didn't feel she was expressing herself fully.
years.xp: Davis added that she had been lighting herself on fire at the time. Indy Week reported that Newton went on to start a band with Rjyan Kidwell, who records as Cex.

years.h: Al Burian, Dave Laney and Tim Remis release Challenger's debut
years.p: The side band Challenger put out Give People What They Want in Lethal Doses, a harder rock record that the A.V. Club filed as agit-punk.

years.h: Ominosity, recorded by Steve Albini, on Eyeball Records
years.p: Milemarker's comeback album was recorded by Steve Albini and Greg Norman and released on New Jersey's Eyeball Records. Noah Leger drums, Monika Bukowska and Tim Remis sing.
years.xp:
Indy Week called the sessions chaotic and rushed; Ben Davis, who had left the band, flew in to play synthesizer. Tony Lazzara plays second drums.

Burian told the A.V. Club that once you've done something, repeating it makes little sense.

years.h: Milemarker plays Wetlands in Chapel Hill, then goes quiet
years.p: Indy Week previewed an $8 homecoming show at Wetlands. Dave Laney planned to move back to the Triangle after the tour, and Milemarker did not record or tour again until 2008.

eras.title: Germany, Denmark and Berlin
eras.text: Milemarker never announced a breakup, so it could come back when it liked: a Chapel Hill show and a European tour in 2008. Then Al Burian, who has a German mother and German citizenship, moved to Berlin.

years.h: Milemarker plays Chapel Hill again and tours Germany and Denmark
years.p: Punknews announced the reunion in May 2008. Indy Week marked Milemarker's first show in two years, and a 12-date European tour included a festival in Lärz, Germany.

years.h: Al Burian moves to Berlin; PM Press collects Burn Collector
years.p: Al Burian moved from Chicago to Berlin in spring 2010. That fall PM Press reprinted Burn Collector issues 1 to 9, his autobiographical zine about travel and bad apartments.
years.xp: Burian told Creative Loafing he grew up speaking German and holds German citizenship through his mother. He tells artists he's a musician and musicians he's a writer.

years.h: Dave Laney's new band Bee Control
years.p: Punknews premiered Bee Control, Dave Laney's project with [[Pelican|5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236]] guitarist Trevor de Brauw and Theo Katsaounis of [[Joan of Arc|0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee]].

eras.title: Overseas
eras.text: A short European reunion tour in 2015 turned into new songs, Milemarker's first album in eleven years, and a U.S. tour at a moment when its dystopian themes suddenly sounded current.

years.h: A European reunion tour and the Conditional Love 7-inch
years.p: A short European tour in 2015 got Al Burian and Dave Laney writing again, and Lovitt Records released the Conditional Love 7-inch, Milemarker's first new music in a decade.

q: We're not At the Drive-In getting back together, you know?
years.h: Overseas, Milemarker's first album in eleven years
years.p: Burian and Laney, now living in Germany, made it with drummer Ezra Cale and keyboardist Lena Kilkka. The title points at their move abroad; one song is named for Carrboro, next to Chapel Hill.

years.h: Milemarker tours the U.S. again, twenty years in
years.p: Milemarker's U.S. tour reached Denver's Marquis Theater. Al Burian told Westword a lot of Milemarker's dystopian themes resonate right now.
